container_info.description: This project aims to develop a comprehensive functional test plan for Wi-Fi 7 (IEEE 802.11be) devices, focusing on non-performance aspects. The plan will cover Multi-Link Operation (MLO) with mandatory Multi-Link Single Radio (MLSR) and optional Multi-Link Multi Radio (MLMR) scenarios, security validation for WPA2 and WPA3 protocols, and basic stability test cases. The outcome will be a structured, reusable test plan suitable for device certification, QA, and interoperability testing.
container_info.reasoning: The project is for producing a structured, reusable functional test plan and related tooling for Wi‑Fi device testing — a backend service (APIs, documentation generation, test orchestration) is the appropriate platform. The container is labeled 'backend' and already includes server-side runtimes and tools (python3, python3-pip, uvicorn, flask, celery, redis, postgresql, mongodb) indicating a Python-based backend environment. Flask is a lightweight Python web framework already present in the image, suitable for simple APIs, documentation endpoints, and orchestration tasks in a headless container following the minimal/lightweight principles.
requirements: virtualenv or venv for isolated environment (venv)
Flask (lightweight web framework) installed via pip (if not already present)
gunicorn or use Flask's built-in dev server / uvicorn for ASGI if using async (uvicorn is present)
minimal requirements.txt containing Flask and any small dependencies (e.g., requests, pyyaml) required by the test plan tooling
simple SQLite database (python built-in sqlite3) for lightweight, file-based storage for test metadata (avoid PostgreSQL/MySQL unless needed)
basic CLI tooling scripts (Python) for orchestrating test runs; no GUI or web frontend required
lightweight task queue if asynchronous jobs needed: Celery with Redis (both present) but only configure for dev with local Redis; otherwise use simple multiprocessing/threading
sphinx or mkdocs (present) for generating documentation; minimal config files
pytest (or unittest) for minimal automated tests — lightweight installation via pip
environment variables for config (no production secrets), and a simple entrypoint script to launch the Flask app in dev mode

steps.name: environment: system prerequisites & idempotent global env
steps.description: Verify python3 and python3 -m pip mapping, ensure python3-venv available, verify redis availability (non-fatal), and create an idempotent /etc/profile.d fragment that exports WORKSPACE, FLASK_ENV and prepends the workspace venv bin to PATH so venv CLIs persist in future shells. Operates in workspace: /home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
command -v python3 >/dev/null || { echo "python3 not found" >&2; exit 2; }
python3 -m pip --version >/dev/null || { echo "python3 pip module not usable" >&2; exit 3; }
# ensure venv module available only if needed
if ! python3 -c "import venv" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq python3-venv
fi
# verify redis availability but DO NOT attempt to start system services here
if command -v redis-cli >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if redis-cli ping >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    :
  else
    echo "warning: redis-cli installed but redis-server not responding on localhost:6379; start redis manually if Celery is required" >&2
  fi
else
  echo "note: redis-cli not found; redis functionality may be unavailable" >&2
fi
# create idempotent /etc/profile.d fragment that prepends venv bin to PATH
PROFILE=/etc/profile.d/coredoc_gov_hub.sh
TMP=$(mktemp)
cat >"$TMP" <<'EOF'
# CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub workspace globals (idempotent)
export WORKSPACE='$WS'
export FLASK_ENV=development
# prepend workspace venv bin to PATH if present
if [ -d "$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin" ] && [[ ":$PATH:" != *":$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin:"* ]]; then
  export PATH="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin:$PATH"
fi
EOF
# compare and install idempotently
if sudo test -f "$PROFILE" && sudo cmp -s "$PROFILE" "$TMP"; then
  rm -f "$TMP"
else
  sudo mv "$TMP" "$PROFILE" && sudo chmod 644 "$PROFILE"
fi
# quick sanity
python3 -V >/dev/null
python3 -m pip --version >/dev/null

steps.name: scaffolding: project layout, venv, deterministic app entrypoint
steps.description: Create the workspace layout, create or reuse a Python venv (.venv) using system python3, verify the venv python works, create a proper Python package under app (with __init__.py), deterministic Flask WSGI entrypoint, absolute-path-safe app/db.py, CLI test runner, minimal docs, requirements.txt with recommended pin ranges, README, .gitignore, .env.example and a start wrapper that uses venv-local gunicorn (or falls back to flask) and writes a pidfile. Operates in workspace: /home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
mkdir -p "$WS" && cd "$WS"
# create venv if missing
if [ ! -d "$WS/.venv" ]; then
  python3 -m venv "$WS/.venv"
fi
VENV_PY="$WS/.venv/bin/python"
[ -x "$VENV_PY" ] || { echo "venv python missing" >&2; exit 4; }
"$VENV_PY" -m pip --version >/dev/null || { echo "venv pip unusable" >&2; exit 5; }
# project layout
mkdir -p app cli docs/source tests data
# package files
cat >app/__init__.py <<'PY'
# app package
PY
cat >app/main.py <<'PY'
from flask import Flask
app = Flask(__name__)
from . import routes  # registers routes
PY
cat >app/routes.py <<'PY'
from .main import app

@app.route('/')
def index():
    return {'status': 'ok', 'app': 'CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub'}
PY
cat >app/db.py <<'PY'
import sqlite3, os
PKG_ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..'))
DB_PATH = os.path.join(PKG_ROOT, 'data', 'coredoc.db')

def get_conn(path=None):
    db = path or DB_PATH
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(db), exist_ok=True)
    return sqlite3.connect(db, check_same_thread=False)
PY
cat >app/celery_app.py <<'PY'
from celery import Celery
import os
broker = os.environ.get('CELERY_BROKER_URL', 'redis://localhost:6379/0')
celery = Celery('coredoc', broker=broker)
PY
cat >cli/run_tests.py <<'PY'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys
import pytest
sys.exit(pytest.main(["-q"]))
PY
chmod +x cli/run_tests.py
# start wrapper - will use venv-local gunicorn if present
cat >start.sh <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="$WS"
VENV_BIN="$WS/.venv/bin"
GUNICORN="$VENV_BIN/gunicorn"
PIDFILE="$WS/.venv/gunicorn.pid"
LOGFILE="$WS/.venv/gunicorn.log"
cd "$WS"
export FLASK_ENV=development
if [ -x "$GUNICORN" ]; then
  # run in new process session so children are grouped
  setsid "$GUNICORN" --bind 127.0.0.1:8000 --pid "$PIDFILE" app.main:app --log-level warning >"$LOGFILE" 2>&1 &
  echo $! > "$WS/.venv/.starter_pid"
  exit 0
else
  # fallback to flask run (uses system python in venv PATH)
  python3 -m flask --app app.main run --host=127.0.0.1 --port=8000 --no-reload >"$LOGFILE" 2>&1 &
  echo $! > "$WS/.venv/.starter_pid"
  exit 0
fi
SH
chmod +x start.sh
# .gitignore and .env.example
cat >.gitignore <<'GI'
.venv/
*.pyc
__pycache__/
data/*.db
.vscode/
GI
cat >.env.example <<'EN'
FLASK_ENV=development
CELERY_BROKER_URL=redis://localhost:6379/0
EN
# requirements with recommended minimal ranges for reproducibility
cat >requirements.txt <<'TXT'
Flask>=2.2,<3.0
requests>=2.28,<3.0
PyYAML>=6.0,<7.0
pytest>=7.0,<8.0
gunicorn>=20.1,<21.0
TXT
cat >docs/conf.py <<'PY'
project = 'CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub'
extensions = []
PY
cat >README.md <<'MD'
Development: activate venv (source .venv/bin/activate) or rely on PATH exported via /etc/profile.d. Start dev server with './start.sh'. Do not commit .venv or data/*.db. For dev Celery: use CELERY_BROKER_URL from .env.example and run '.venv/bin/celery -A app.celery_app worker --loglevel=info' (requires redis).
MD

steps.description: Initialize a minimal SQLite database at data/coredoc.db using the workspace venv python so schema tooling uses the same environment. Creates a 'tests' table if missing. Operates in workspace: /home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
mkdir -p "$WS/data"
VENV_PY="$WS/.venv/bin/python"
[ -x "$VENV_PY" ] || { echo "venv python missing" >&2; exit 4; }
DBPATH="$WS/data/coredoc.db"
if [ ! -f "$DBPATH" ]; then
  export DBPATH
  "$VENV_PY" - <<'PY'
import os, sqlite3
DB = os.environ['DBPATH']
conn = sqlite3.connect(DB)
cur = conn.cursor()
cur.execute('''CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tests (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, status TEXT, created_ts TEXT)''')
conn.commit()
conn.close()
print('initialized')
PY
fi

steps.name: validation: start app (isolated), poll-ready, smoke test, run pytest, and clean stop (process-group safe)
steps.description: Start the app using venv-local gunicorn (or fallback to uvicorn/flask) in its own process session so worker processes are grouped. Poll the HTTP endpoint until ready with timeout (capture logs on failure), run pytest (venv-local), then stop the server deterministically by killing the process group (negative PGID) to ensure worker cleanup. Operates in workspace: /home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub and depends on all prior steps.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
VENV_BIN="$WS/.venv/bin"
GUNICORN="$VENV_BIN/gunicorn"
UVICORN="$VENV_BIN/uvicorn"
PYTEST="$VENV_BIN/pytest"
PIDFILE="$WS/.venv/gunicorn.pid"
LOGFILE="$WS/.venv/gunicorn.log"
cd "$WS"
# choose server: prefer gunicorn, fallback to uvicorn, then flask
SERVER_TYPE=""
if [ -x "$GUNICORN" ]; then SERVER_TYPE=gunicorn; fi
if [ -z "$SERVER_TYPE" ] && [ -x "$UVICORN" ]; then SERVER_TYPE=uvicorn; fi
if [ -z "$SERVER_TYPE" ]; then SERVER_TYPE=flask; fi
# ensure no stale pid
[ -f "$PIDFILE" ] && rm -f "$PIDFILE" || true
RETRIES=60
SLEEP=0.5
READY=0
SERVER_PID=0
case "$SERVER_TYPE" in
  gunicorn)
    # start gunicorn in new session (setsid) so children share PGID
    LOGFILE="$LOGFILE"
    setsid "$GUNICORN" --bind 127.0.0.1:8000 --pid "$PIDFILE" app.main:app --worker-tmp-dir /dev/shm --log-level warning >"$LOGFILE" 2>&1 &
    SERVER_PID=$!
    ;;
  uvicorn)
    LOGFILE="$WS/.venv/uvicorn.log"
    setsid "$UVICORN" app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 >"$LOGFILE" 2>&1 &
    SERVER_PID=$!
    ;;
  flask)
    LOGFILE="$WS/.venv/flask.log"
    setsid python3 -m flask --app app.main run --host=127.0.0.1 --port=8000 --no-reload >"$LOGFILE" 2>&1 &
    SERVER_PID=$!
    ;;
esac
# wait for readiness
for i in $(seq 1 $RETRIES); do
  if curl -sS -f http://127.0.0.1:8000/ >/dev/null 2>&1; then READY=1; break; fi
  sleep $SLEEP
done
if [ "$READY" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "server failed to become ready; dumping logs (first 200 lines):" >&2
  [ -f "$LOGFILE" ] && sed -n '1,200p' "$LOGFILE" >&2 || true
  # try to cleanup
  if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
    PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$PID" ]; then
      PGID=$(ps -o pgid= "$PID" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)
      if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then kill -TERM -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
    fi
  else
    kill -TERM "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  exit 6
fi
# smoke test
curl -sS -f http://127.0.0.1:8000/ >/dev/null
# run pytest via venv-local
"$PYTEST" -q "$WS/tests"
# shutdown: prefer pidfile PGID, else server pid PGID
if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
  PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE")
  PGID=$(ps -o pgid= "$PID" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)
  if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then
    kill -TERM -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true
    sleep 0.5
    kill -KILL -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true
  else
    kill -TERM "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    sleep 0.5
    kill -KILL "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  rm -f "$PIDFILE" || true
else
  if [ -n "$SERVER_PID" ] && ps -p "$SERVER_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    PGID=$(ps -o pgid= "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)
    if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then
      kill -TERM -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true
      sleep 0.5
      kill -KILL -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true
    else
      kill -TERM "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
      sleep 0.5
      kill -KILL "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
  fi
fi
wait 2>/dev/null || true
echo "validation: success"
